findings.title: Platform selection does not implement the promised hardware fallback
findings.description: `_select_arch()` chooses CUDA or Metal based on the operating system, not whether that device is available. On Linux without a CUDA driver, for example, it still selects `qd.cuda`; the Open Notes say `qd.init()` then raises and the server exits. That conflicts with A7 and the slice-plan requirement that a host without Metal or CUDA warn and fall back to `qd.cpu`. Detect device availability and use the fallback, or narrow the stated requirement.

findings.title: Reflect bounds changes are not synchronized back to GPU state
findings.description: The design exports positions and velocities, then applies bounds policy to both arrays. But the specified notification and upload mechanism only handles positions (`notify_positions_modified()` and `upload_positions()`). `REFLECT` changes velocity as well as position; without uploading the changed velocities, the next GPU tick retains the pre-reflection velocity. This leaves A4’s reflect behavior unmet. Synchronize the modified velocities too, or handle reflection on the GPU.

findings.title: The GPU path does not define how SOFT bounds are applied
findings.description: The design treats SOFT like WRAP and REFLECT: it describes post-tick bounds enforcement and position sync-back. But slice 314 defines SOFT as a repulsive force in the force pipeline, not a position correction. The proposed GPU setup and fused tick do not specify how that force reaches the kernel. As written, the four-policy success criterion does not establish SOFT behavior. Specify how the GPU path implements the SOFT force, or explicitly defer SOFT and revise the required scope and criterion.

findings.title: GPU transfer and synchronization hangs have no handling strategy
findings.description: The new path relies on host-device transfers (`from_numpy()` and exports) and `qd.sync()` during ticks. The notes define startup error handling and say post-start GPU failures are fatal, but do not define what happens if a transfer or synchronization hangs, or how a runtime device failure is detected and handled. Specify a bounded timeout or an explicit process-fatal strategy that prevents the server from hanging indefinitely.
